\section{Experiments}\label{sec:experiments}

The experiments ask what Proposition~\ref{prop:guarantee} certifies on
surrogates that were never built to satisfy Definition~\ref{def:eta}, and how
far that certificate sits below what predictive greedy delivers.  The
certificate is read at the measured selection error $\etasel$ of the finished
run (Remark~\ref{rem:etasel-measurable}).  Three surrogate families are
ordered by their distance from the model of Section~\ref{sec:model}:
surrogates \emph{learned} from data, surrogates that evaluate the same
objective on a \emph{partially observed} input, and \emph{heuristic}
surrogates for a true objective that itself lies outside the model.  The
instances constructed for Theorems~\ref{thm:exact} and~\ref{thm:tightness}
are run through the same pipeline as a control.

\paragraph{Setup.}
In every family $f$ is the quantity of interest, $\tilde f$ is what the
algorithm may query, and nothing synthetic is inserted between them.
\emph{(E1) Feature selection:} $f(S)$ is the held-out accuracy of a decision
tree trained on the features $S$, and $\tilde f(S)$ the mean
\EOneCVFolds-fold cross-validation accuracy of the same estimator on the
training split alone, so the held-out split is structurally out of the
predictor's reach; \EOneNumDatasets\ datasets (the largest with
\EOneAirlineRows\ rows), \EOneNumSeeds\ splits each,
$K=\EOneKMin,\dots,\EOneKMain$.
\emph{(E2) Influence maximization:} $f$ is one-hop coverage in a network and
$\tilde f$ the same coverage on an observed graph keeping each edge
independently with probability $p\in\{\ETwoPSet\}$
\citep{kempe2003maximizing}; \ETwoNumGraphs\ networks (largest
\ETwoLargestNodes\ nodes, \ETwoLargestEdges\ edges), \ETwoNumSeedsPerP\
observed graphs per network and $p$, giving \ETwoNumTrajectories\
trajectories of length \ETwoKMain\
\citep{rozemberczki2019gemsec,leskovec2007graph,yin2017local}.
\emph{(E3) Extractive summarization:} $f$ is the ROUGE-1 F score against a
reference summary and $\tilde f$ one of \EThreeNumSurrogates\ standard
submodular sentence-selection objectives that never see the reference
\citep{lin2011class}; \EThreeNumDocs\ articles in \EThreeNumCategories\
categories, $K=\EThreeKMin,\dots,\EThreeKMax$.  Ratios are
$f(S^{\tilde f})/f(S^{f})$, whose denominator is greedy on the true
objective and hence an upper-estimate proxy for the optimum
(Table~\ref{tab:experiments}, note~(i)); on the one dataset small enough to
enumerate the optimum, that proxy inflates a ratio by
\EOneBreastOptInflationPct\,\%.  Greedy uses cached lazy evaluation;
accelerated variants carry guarantees of their own
\citep{mirzasoleiman2015lazier} but are not used, because measuring $\etasel$
needs the exact per-step maximizer of the true gain.
Appendix~\ref{app:experiments} gives the protocol, the baseline panel and the
enumeration.

\paragraph{Learned surrogates.}
At $K=\EOneKMain$, over \EOneNumRunsKMain\ runs, the median ratio is
\EOneKMainRatioMedian\ (interquartile range \EOneKMainRatioLoQ\ to
\EOneKMainRatioHiQ) at median selection error \EOneKMainEtaSelMedian, so the
median run certifies $L_{\EOneKMain}(\etasel)=\EOneKMainBound$ against an
exact worst case of $\rho_{\EOneKMain}=\EOneKMainExactWorst$ at that same
error; on the largest dataset alone the ratio is \EOneAirlineRatioMedian\ at
error \EOneAirlineEtaSelMedian, certifying \EOneAirlineBound.  Which measure
the guarantee is read at decides whether it says anything: the trajectory
error of the same runs has median at least \EOneKMainEtaTrMedian\ (the
reported figure discards candidate pairs whose gains fall below one
quantization unit of the accuracy, so it is a lower estimate;
Appendix~\ref{app:experiments}), and at that value
Proposition~\ref{prop:guarantee} certifies only \EOneKMainEtaTrBound.

\paragraph{Partially observed surrogates.}
Here $f$ and $\tilde f$ are one function of two nested edge sets, so the
predictor errs only by missing coverage.  At $K=\ETwoKMain$ the median ratio
is \ETwoKMainRatioMedian\ (interquartile range \ETwoKMainRatioLoQ\ to
\ETwoKMainRatioHiQ) at median selection error \ETwoKMainEtaSelMedian,
certifying $L_{\ETwoKMain}(\etasel)=\ETwoKMainBound$ against an exact worst
case of \ETwoKMainExactWorst.  Only \ETwoNonposPctKMain\,\%\ of steps have a
nonpositive chosen true gain, and no predicted and true gain can disagree in
sign, both by construction rather than by luck
(Table~\ref{tab:experiments}, note~(iii)).

\paragraph{Observation probability against error.}
This family lets the amount of error be dialled.  Lowering $p$ from
\ETwoPHigh\ to \ETwoPLow\ raises the median $\etasel$ monotonically on all
\ETwoNumGraphsEtaMonotone\ networks, by factors from \ETwoEtaRiseMin\ to
\ETwoEtaRiseMax; the realized ratio degrades far more slowly over the same
range, also monotonically on all \ETwoNumGraphsRatioMonotone\ networks, from
no worse than \ETwoRatioPHighMin\ down to between \ETwoRatioPLowMin\ and
\ETwoRatioPLowMax.  The certified bound moves fastest of the three:
$L_{\ETwoKMain}(\etasel)$ falls from the range \ETwoBoundPHighMin\ to
\ETwoBoundPHighMax\ down to \ETwoBoundPLowMin\ to \ETwoBoundPLowMax, by up to
a factor \ETwoBoundDropFactorMax\ on one network.  Missing observations
therefore cost much less realized value than they cost certificate.

\paragraph{Heuristic surrogates outside the model.}
At $K=\EThreeKMain$, over \EThreeNumRunsKMain\ runs, the median ratio falls
to \EThreeKMainRatioMedian\ (interquartile range \EThreeKMainRatioLoQ\ to
\EThreeKMainRatioHiQ) at median selection error \EThreeKMainEtaSelMedian,
where $L_{\EThreeKMain}(\etasel)=\EThreeKMainBound$ and the exact worst case
is \EThreeKMainExactWorst; the best single surrogate, the
\EThreeBestSurrogateName\ objective, reaches \EThreeBestSurrogateRatio.
Across the three families the median selection
error grows and the median ratio falls together, which is the spectrum
Table~\ref{tab:experiments} summarizes.

\paragraph{An out-of-model finding.}
The true objective of the third family does not satisfy the hypotheses of
Proposition~\ref{prop:guarantee}, and we measure by how much rather than
leaving it implicit.  On \EThreeStructTriples\ triples
$(A,\,A\cup\{b\},\,e)$ drawn from the articles with
$|A|\le\EThreeStructMaxSetSize$, the ROUGE-1 F score violates
submodularity on \EThreeSubmodViolPct\,\%\ and monotonicity on
\EThreeMonoViolPct\,\%\ of them, the largest submodularity violation being
\EThreeMaxSubmodViol\ in units of the score, while the
\EThreeNumSurrogates\ surrogates record \EThreeSurrogateViolCount\
violations of either property on the same triples; a further
\EThreeNonposPctKMain\,\%\ of trajectory steps have a nonpositive chosen true
gain and fall outside the scope of $\etasel$
(Table~\ref{tab:experiments}, note~(ii)).  For this family the $L_K$ column
is therefore a reference value computed by the same formula and not a
certificate, and recovering one would need a guarantee stated for
approximately submodular objectives (Section~\ref{sec:related}).

\paragraph{The worst case, executed by the same code.}
\EFourNumInstances\ constructed instances were run through the pipeline that
produced every other point: \EFourNumVjInstances\ instances of the $V_j$
family of Theorem~\ref{thm:exact}, one per segment at $K\in\{\EFourKList\}$,
and \EFourNumUKInstances\ of the per-$K$ family of
Theorem~\ref{thm:tightness}.  Realized ratios match the theoretical values to
$\EFourMaxDeviation$, and on the $V_j$ instances the measured selection error
matches the design error to $\EFourEtaSelDeviation$.  The worst case is thus
not an asymptotic figure of speech: it occurs point by point in the same
implementation of greedy that produced the scatter, so the vertical distance
in Figure~\ref{fig:money} between the crosses and the colored points at a
common $\etasel$ is a distance between two behaviours of one algorithm, not
between two measurement paths.  Three auxiliary figures, the distribution of
$\etasel$ by budget, the observation probability sweep, and the true against
predicted gains with an error band drawn in, are deferred to
Appendix~\ref{app:experiments}.
